claims.text: The baseline material is a single-phase FCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is addition of 5 at.% Al.
Adding 5 at.% Al will cause coherent precipitates to form.
The coherent precipitates will provide precipitate strengthening.
Al addition will provide solid-solution strengthening.
Adding 5 at.% Al will improve high-temperature yield strength by 20% relative to the Al-free baseline.
The predicted improvement will hold at 1000°C under a stated load of 100 MPa.
The density increase caused by the intervention will be less than 2%.
Room-temperature yield strength after Al addition will remain within 5% of the baseline value.
The exact morphology and distribution of the proposed precipitates are uncertain.
The hypothesis will be tested by tensile testing at 1000°C with a stated 100 MPa loading condition.
The experiment will measure yield strength, density, and microstructure.
A yield-strength improvement below 10% will falsify the hypothesis.
A density increase above 3% will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires a 20% yield-strength improvement, but only an improvement below 10% is defined as falsifying. Results from 10% to below 20% would violate the stated prediction without falsifying it.
The boundary requires density increase below 2%, whereas falsification occurs only above 3%. A density increase from 2% through 3% would violate the boundary but would not falsify the hypothesis.

Yield strength normally requires a stress-ramped test, while the experiment is described as tensile testing with a fixed 100 MPa load. The stated loading protocol is therefore not clearly aligned with the claimed yield-strength outcome.
